data.title: Collapse
data.tagline: Hide secondary details until the user asks for them
data.description: A collapse panel shows a heading first and expands the body on request. It suits FAQs and advanced settings. Do not hide warnings, required rules, or anything people must see before they act.

distinctions.label: Accordion
distinctions.explanation: A collapse panel is any content that can expand and close. An accordion is usually a group of collapse panels and often allows only one open panel at a time.

use: Optional sections in a compact page
avoid: Hide critical information or a required action
Nest several levels of collapsible panels
Make the heading too vague to predict the content
Collapse everything when most people need it open

lessonPractice.title: A purchase page has 20 common questions, but Refund requests must be submitted within 7 days directly affects the decision. How should it be arranged?

options.label: Collapse answers on demand but keep the seven-day rule visible near the purchase action
options.feedback: Collapsing reduces the cost of secondary content, while a decision-critical condition should not depend on discovery.

options.label: Collapse every answer and refund condition by default and show only the 20 questions
options.feedback: The page becomes shorter but hides a key purchase condition, so users may decide without seeing the limit.

options.label: Turn all 20 questions into one row of tabs and show one answer at a time
options.feedback: Many tabs are difficult to scan and wrap, and they still fail to keep the refund condition visible.

data.agentPrompt: Organize FAQ answers as collapsible panels, but keep the seven-day refund window persistently visible near price and purchase controls. Make each heading summarize its answer, then test keyboard toggling and long mobile question wrapping.
